case.subject: Microsoft Disability Answer Desk and Be My Eyes
case.tool: Be My Eyes Service AI and Service Connect
case.problem: Blind and low-vision customers can struggle to describe a technical problem they cannot see.
case.workflow: The app connects customers to an AI assistant trained on Microsoft products; camera-based live support also lets the human support team see the problem.
case.result: Be My Eyes reports 61% of requests resolved solely by its Smart Agent and a 47% reduction in average handling time.
case.result_basis: Vendor case study; not an independent evaluation.
case.measurement_context: The page gives no sample size, measurement dates or controlled-study method. Do not extrapolate these figures to all users or attribute the whole service's speed improvement solely to AI.
case.case_date: Undated historical case study, accessed October 23, 2026; not today's launch.
case.source_quote: customers can now resolve their technical issues in half the time compared with traditional voice-only support
case.limitation: Keep human support available. A vendor's resolution metric does not prove every answer correct.
case.listener_action: Suggested experiment: identify one inaccessible support step and test it with affected users, measuring successful resolution and ease of reaching a human.
case.availability: The current vendor page lists the Microsoft integration and Service AI/Service Connect. Eligibility and individual access were not tested.
